notes: Bug fixtures are forward diffs of the commits that introduced each known bug (git diff <commit>^ <commit>), found by searching the history for the buggy code and checking that the bug is present in the commit's tree and absent before it. Unlike v1's reverse diffs of fixes, no removed line carries a fix's comment.

Each diff excludes tests/, docs/ and *.md. A commit over the input limit is scoped to the file(s) holding its bug ('scope'); a bug whose file alone is over the limit is left out (static_batch_replay), as is a bug whose cause is outside any reviewable diff (unsubscribed_rows_freeze: real gauges reading every row arrived as 60.8K of QML in 40e51ce).
The proposal is the commit's own subject line: what the author said the change does.

base_rev is the tree the diff applies to, and repo_context.json is its --no-llm index. post_rev is the commit; score claims against it. A real bug present in the post-state but not introduced by the diff is not a known bug of the fixture; label it as such.
The clean fixtures are v1's, unchanged apart from the proposal.

known_bugs.summary: qttune_decode_signal is called with a hardcoded length of 8 instead of the frame's data_length, so short frames decode bytes past their payload and CAN FD frames lose signals beyond byte 8.
handleFrameInternal clears m_stagingBuffer before decoding each frame, so the coalesced batch carries only the last frame's signals and every other frame's values in the 100 ms window are lost.
Drops are counted in onFrame but reported only from handleFrameInternal, which does not run while the backlog is saturated, so the user is never told about drops while they happen.

known_bugs.summary: onFrame reads m_currentFrameCount on the worker thread while handleFrameInternal increments it on the GUI thread; the int is not atomic, a data race.

The backpressure check compares the cumulative m_currentFrameCount with MaxFrames, and the count only resets on connect, so after 10,000 frames every frame is dropped at the source for the rest of the session; drops are reported only from handleFrameInternal, which then never runs, so the drop count stops updating too.
payloadHex reads data_length bytes of the 64-byte inline buffer without clamping, so a transport reporting a longer length makes the bridge read past the buffer.
